function.name: mcp__vornik__document_get_metadata
function.description: [vornik] Return the operator-visible metadata for an attached document (title, author, publisher, ISBN, language, section count, MIME type, extractor version). Returns a small JSON blob — use BEFORE reading sections so you know the structure exists.

artifact_id.description: Source artifact ID (typically email-att-... from the [Attached files] block).

function.name: mcp__vornik__document_get_outline
function.description: [vornik] Return the document's table of contents — a flat list of {section_id, title, depth, text_bytes} entries in reading order. Use this to decide which sections to read in detail instead of dumping the whole document into context.

function.name: mcp__vornik__document_read_section
function.description: [vornik] Read one section's text content (markdown). Bounded by limit_chars (default 8000). For very large sections, page through by passing the next_offset returned in the previous response.

offset_chars.description: Character offset to start reading from. Default 0.

function.name: mcp__consult__vornik_architecture
function.description: Vornik architecture source of truth: how the daemon, executor, workflows, memory/RAG, channels, and the A2A surface are designed and why. Ask one clear question; get a grounded, cited answer.

question.description: The question to ask the domain expert. One clear question.

function.name: mcp__vornik__grant_step_tools
function.description: Narrow which MCP tools a step of THIS execution is offered, to keep its prompt small. Pass the tools that step actually needs. You can only ever narrow within what the role is already permitted — you cannot grant a tool the role lacks, and the request is refused if it names one. Call again with a superset to escalate if a step turns out to need more (limited attempts per step).

step_id.description: Step to scope. Defaults to the current step.

tools.description: A SUBSET of the tools you already have available in this step, named exactly as they appear in your tool list. This narrows what a step is offered; it cannot add a tool you do not already hold, and naming one refuses the whole request. Do not guess at names.

escalation.description: True when widening an earlier grant for the same step.
